title: bl_land.ops_no_work_rows warns 'landed with no work rows' for every Agent-tool worker, whose capture writes agent rows, not a branch row
goal: Found in the SP-s5fdczv7 review: BG-m6fknqr5 made ops_no_work_rows look only for a worker's branch row, the row a headless worker session writes at its first prompt; a kb-worker started with the Agent tool (kb-sprint run step 3's default) runs inside the orchestrator's session, writes agent-start and agent-stop rows naming the item (ql_capture.agent_row, its directory on work/<id>) and never a branch row, and at land time the orchestrator's session is still open so no sidecar line exists, so every Agent-tool landing prints the no-work-rows warning although capture worked. ops_no_work_rows also counts an agent-start or agent-stop row of the item or a descendant as a worker's capture, still not the orchestrator's claim, done or release; the repro (a spool with only agent rows of the item) exits 0, and backlog.md and tools.md say which rows count.

run: import os,sys,tempfile;from pathlib import Path;t=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp());os.environ['CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA']=str(t/'d');os.environ['CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT']=str(Path.cwd());sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import ql_capture as q,bl_land as b;q.record('work','s1',prompt_id='p1',agent_id='a1',item='ST-aaaaaaaa',action='agent-start');q.record('work','s1',prompt_id='p2',agent_id='a1',item='ST-aaaaaaaa',action='agent-stop');r=b.ops_no_work_rows(Path.cwd(),'ST-aaaaaaaa');print('warns although a subagent worked:',r);sys.exit(1 if r else 0)
